newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine traders say wheat needs more rain.
newsitem.headline: Argentine traders say wheat needs more rain.

text.p: Rain fell throughout much of Argentina's wheat belt Wednesday, following rains on Sunday and Monday, but farmers in drought-hit zones need still more to be sure of sowing, traders said.

"Obviously it is good, but it is not enough," one trader told Reuters. He said that falls of up to 50 millimeters had been registered in some parts of Cordoba -- one of the areas worst hit by dryness -- but other parts of the province had seen hardly any rain.
Another area affected by the past four months of dryish weather, Santa Fe, received more rain, he said.
Another trader believed that more rain was needed to bring moisture levels up to par in northern Buenos Aires, southern Santa Fe and Cordoba.
"We'll have to see if it continues raining until the weekend. Sincerely we need more rain" he said. "There are farmers in Cordoba who are asking themselves whether they are going to be able to sow."
He said that the dry areas needed about 70 millimeters to get back into sowing shape.

Traders disagreed about whether area sown with wheat would fall much this season from 1996/97. One said that sowing should be more or less stable from last season unless January wheat prices fall considerably.

Heavy rain throughout much of Argentina's wheat belt Sunday and Monday and Sparks South America Vice-president Juan Martin Rebolini told Reuters that it seemed enough to make sure that sowing did not fall by more than 10 percent from 1996/97.
But most of the rain fell in Buenos Aires province, with the heaviest falls in the north. Argentina's main wheat producing area is southern Buenos Aires, which has not been much affected by dryness.
Sowing of longer-cycle wheat in northern areas is due to start later this month, but much of the sowing in the south takes place in July.
Weather Services Corporation Wednesday forecast finer weather for Thursday and Friday.
Rebolini said in April that Sparks expected Argentina's wheat area to fall by 10 percent from 1996/97, leading to production of 12.7-13.3 million tonnes in normal conditions.
Farmers sowed 7.2 million hectares last season, and produced a record 15.8 million tonnes.
Sparks South America is the local office of U.S. agricultural consultant Sparks Companies, of Memphis, Tenn.
